rule: R6 Stack: R1 (first c/w look 2-360 min before start with listed EV >= 2.5%) and first seen inside the window (m0 <= 360) and plus-money (cost < 0.50)
numbers_reproduced: Reproduced with the shared loader and the builder's expr: 119 bets, 40 games, 74 with a close in 32 games. CLV (closeFair/cost-1 at the look) +3.21% [+2.30%, +4.53%] game-clustered (builder [+2.33%, +4.45%]; seed difference only); 81% beat the close; close_ok 71 closes/31 games +3.21% [+2.32%, +4.51%]. R1: 184 bets, 44 games, 116 closes/40 games, +2.54% [+1.77%, +3.52%]. ROI (114 settled WON/LOST, 38 games) -2.9% at the look price, -3.1% at the first-listed price, CI about [-27%, +23%]: uninformative (iid SE of ROI about 11 pts; a true +3% edge is 0.5 sigma away). Builder's halves reproduced exactly: decision day Oct 3 = 16 closes/16 games +2.43%; Oct 4-5 = 58 closes/22 games +3.43%. The loader's game-balanced date split (cut Oct 4) gives 62 closes/28 games +3.11% vs 12 closes/4 games +3.75%: the 'second half' is 12 closes in 4 games. By first day stack vs rest of R1: Oct 3 +2.43% (16) vs +1.73% (15); Oct 4 +3.34% (46) vs +0.62% (21); Oct 5 +3.75% (12) vs +3.11% (6): stack ahead on each day and in both start-time halves (28 closes +3.26% vs 47 closes... early half rest +1.15%; late half 46 closes +3.18% vs rest +1.55%). Matches the builder's headline; the disagreement is in how much of it is luck and how much is the stack rather than the EV gate.
reason: R1 is real, but R6's extra value over R1 is not distinguishable from selection luck, and 70% of its CLV rests on one close source. (1) Added value over R1 is only +0.67 pts (3.21% vs 2.54%) for dropping 65 of 184 bets. Raw p against random same-size subsets of R1's closes (20000 draws): 0.0053 bet-level (99.5th percentile), 0.0070 shuffling CLV within first-day, 0.0213 when whole games are drawn (clusters kept). Data-snooping across a 1200-cell grid of the same kind of rule (EV gate 1-5% x window 60-360 x freshness x price cut; 221-461 variants with >=40-74 closes), White reality check on gain-over-R1 with game bootstrap (5000): family-wise p for R6's own gain = 0.20 (n>=74), 0.28 (n>=60), 0.51 (n>=40); studentized 0.20-0.25; the best variant in the family (EV gate 3-3.5%, window 240, cost<0.50) has family-wise p 0.05-0.10. Bonferroni on the raw 0.0053: x15 families = 0.08, x522 variants = 1 (2.8); on the game-level raw 0.0213: x15 = 0.32, x522 = 1. (2) At the same sample size a single EV gate does as well: R1 with gate 3.0% = 78 closes, +3.25%, no freshness or price condition; gate 3.0% window 240 = 74 closes +3.38%. 27 of 302 grid variants with >=60 closes have a CLV at or above R6's; R6 ranks 7th of 34 variants with 70-80 closes. (3) Close source: 52 of the 74 closes are Tracker closes (CNO's own books read before the start, only for bets Tj/auto-bet placed): +3.91% on 23 games. The 22 other closes (18 Novig trades, 3 ESPN, 1 Pinnacle) are +1.56% [+0.58%, +3.27%]; the 19 close_ok ones +1.30% [+0.52%, +2.39%] on 14 games (game sign-flip one-sided p 0.008, bootstrap 0.0014; x15 = 0.12, x522 = 1). Against R1's own independent closes (33 closes, 23 games, +0.81%) the stack's independent gain is +0.5 pts, p about 0.12; stack vs rest of R1 within independent closes +1.15 pts, cluster p = 0.31 (19 vs 14 closes). The same tracker-vs-independent gap exists at fixed first-look EV in the whole universe (EV 2.5-4%: tracker +1.9% on 38 closes vs independent -0.2% on 21). (4) The effect is an AND of two conditions, not three additive effects: closes by cell fresh/plus = both 74 +3.21%; fresh only 18 +0.74%; plus only 21 +1.47%; neither 3 +4.48%. Cluster-robust OLS in R1 (116 closes, 40 games): CLV on EV, fresh, plus: fresh +0.89 pts p 0.30, plus +1.40 pts p 0.08, EV p 0.66; the stack dummy +1.67 pts p 0.009 (raw, before any haircut). (5) Missing closes are not random: 45 of 119 stack bets have none (mostly props; 23 notes say Pinnacle's prop close is not in ParlayAPI's file); 98% of placed bets have a close vs 33% of unplaced. CLV is measured on 62% of the rule. What does hold up: the 95% game-clustered CI excludes zero; leave-one-game-out range +3.01% to +3.83%; dropping the 3 most influential games +2.77% [+2.05%, +3.88%]; dropping the 3 biggest games +3.61%; 28 of 32 games positive (game-mean t 6.7); no single game drives it. Verdict: the data suggests R1 (EV gate) is real; the data does not show that the freshness + plus-money cuts add value (the three conditions were picked on the same 2.26 days). Proposal to put to Tj only as a question, not an action: keep R1 and, if anything, test a higher EV gate as one parameter; do not adopt the stack on this evidence.
caveats: My variant family (1200 grid cells, 221-461 usable) is an emulation of the builder's 522 variants, not the same set; the reality-check p for R6's gain is 0.20-0.51 across min-closes choices, so it is 'not significant', not 'proven chance'.

Bootstrap p of 0.0006 for stack-vs-R1 (overlapping groups) is not a valid selection-adjusted p; the builder's 'bootstrap p(stack <= rest of R1) = 0.000' compares the best split against its complement and ignores that the split was chosen.

Tracker closes (CNO books read before the start) share the entry fair's source (CNO consensus) and exist only for placed bets; whether their +3.9% (vs +1.6% on other closes) is a close-source effect or a genuine placed-bet selection effect cannot be separated with this file.
Second half is 12 closes / 4 games (loader split) or 58 closes / 22 games (Oct 4-5 vs Oct 3); neither is an independent test of a rule fitted on the same 2.26 days.
ROI is uninformative: -2.9% on 114 settled / 38 games, CI about [-27%, +23%]; confirming a +3% edge by results needs roughly 6000 bets.

What would settle it: about 220-500 closes per arm (stack vs rest) for a true +0.7 to +1.0 pt gap (bet sd 3.8 pts, 80% power, iid; more with clustering); at about 33 stack closes and 19 rest closes a day that is 3-4 weeks of logging; a prospective pre-registered stack with independent (non-Tracker) closes only needs about 100 closes to separate +1.3% from 0 at 2 sigma.
Proposed changes to rules that decide bets are questions for Tj; nothing here loosens a safety limit.
